question_text: Zinc has five naturally occurring isotopes: $48.63 \%$ of ${ }^{64} \mathrm{Zn}$ with an atomic weight of 63.929 amu; $27.90 \%$ of ${ }^{66} \mathrm{Zn}$ with an atomic weight of 65.926 amu; $4.10 \%$ of ${ }^{67} \mathrm{Zn}$ with an atomic weight of 66.927 amu; $18.75 \%$ of ${ }^{68} \mathrm{Zn}$ with an atomic weight of 67.925 amu; and $0.62 \%$ of ${ }^{70} \mathrm{Zn}$ with an atomic weight of 69.925 amu. Calculate the average atomic weight of Zn .The unit of the answer is amu.
response:
The average atomic weight is the abundance-weighted sum of the isotope masses:

$$\bar{M} = 0.4863(63.929) + 0.2790(65.926) + 0.0410(66.927) + 0.1875(67.925) + 0.0062(69.925)$$

Computing each contribution and summing gives approximately $65.40$ amu.

$$\boxed{65.40}$$
